TensorProduct.VanishesTrivially.{u} (R : Type u) [CommRing R] {M : Type u} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] {N : Type u}
  [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N] {ι : Type u} [Fintype ι] (m : ι → M) (n : ι → N) : Prop
```
***
An expression $\sum_i m_i \otimes n_i$ in $M \otimes N$
*vanishes trivially* if there exist a finite index type $\kappa$,
elements $(y_j)_{j \in \kappa}$ of $N$, and elements $(a_{ij})_{i \in \iota, j \in \kappa}$ of $R$
such that for all $i$,
$$n_i = \sum_j a_{ij} y_j$$
and for all $j$,
$$\sum_{i} a_{ij} m_i = 0.$$
Note that this condition is not symmetric in $M$ and $N$.
(The terminology "trivial" comes from [Stacks 00HK](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00HK).)

`rfl : a = a` is the unique constructor of the equality type. This is the
same as `Eq.refl` except that it takes `a` implicitly instead of explicitly.

This is a more powerful theorem than it may appear at first, because although
the statement of the theorem is `a = a`, Lean will allow anything that is
definitionally equal to that type. So, for instance, `2 + 2 = 4` is proven in
Lean by `rfl`, because both sides are the same up to definitional equality.

***
An expression $\sum_i m_i \otimes n_i$ in $M \otimes N$
*vanishes trivially* if there exist a finite index type $\kappa$,
elements $(y_j)_{j \in \kappa}$ of $N$, and elements $(a_{ij})_{i \in \iota, j \in \kappa}$ of $R$
such that for all $i$,
$$n_i = \sum_j a_{ij} y_j$$
and for all $j$,
$$\sum_{i} a_{ij} m_i = 0.$$
